name_reason: Already conformant: fd2_ prefix, find action, char_at_cursor_pos descriptor. No address residue. Accurately reflects purpose (linear scan of the runtime_char array for the first alive char whose world position equals the cursor world position).
purpose: Locate the first ALIVE runtime character standing on the cursor's world tile (cursor_world_x, cursor_world_y); return its char index, or -1 if no alive char occupies that tile.
logic_summary: Linear scan i = 0 .. data_fd2_battle_party_member_count-1 over data_fd2_battle_runtime_char_array_ptr (stride RUNTIME_CHAR_SIZE = 0x50). For each slot, compare byte[0] (bPos_x) == data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_x AND byte[1] (bPos_y) == data_fd2_battle_cursor_world_y; on a position match, call fd2_check_char_is_dead(i) and, if it reports alive (returns 0), return i immediately. If the loop completes with no alive match, return -1. (Dead chars sharing the tile are skipped, so a corpse under the cursor does not block selection.) The decompiler shows a leading __CHK(0x10) stack-probe thunk inserted by the compiler; it is not game logic.

returns.semantics: Index (0 .. party_member_count-1) of the first ALIVE character whose tile equals the cursor tile, or -1 when none is found. Callers use the index to drive character selection / cursor-target status queries and treat -1 as 'no selectable unit here'.
